gaps: No accessible primary transcription or image of the cited 集成04315 inscription was inspected, so the reading, context, and precise date of that specific 半 example remain unverified here.
The inspected textual pages do not establish an oracle-bone form. Absence from the page is not proof of absence from the full paleographic record.

The component account labels 八 both semantic and phonetic, while its cited phonetic evidence has a substantial final-vowel/coda difference between reconstructed 八 *pˤret and 半 *pˤan-s. The account does not explain that correspondence; the phonetic assignment remains a source assertion.
The exact graphic sequence from bronze forms through seal, clerical, and regular scripts was not independently reconstructed; no glyph images were visually inspected.

The proposed original sense ‘split/cut’ and extension ‘half’ are reported by CUHK and broadly accord with Shuowen, but no dated sequence establishing when the word’s senses changed was found. Do not infer chronology from the order of dictionary glosses.
The assertion that 半 is 判’s initial graph is attributed by CUHK to 何琳儀; the specific textual and phonological demonstration was not inspected.
The Mawangdui 半-for-磐 loan is reported by CUHK, but early attestations for both spoken words and the sound basis beyond the cited correspondence were not independently checked.
No Proto-Sino-Tibetan comparison was verified. The dossier’s proposed *par relationship to 畔 was not established by the sources opened.
Contemporary readings beyond Mandarin bàn were not researched in this pass; the cited modern MOE entry verifies Mandarin only.

No historical glyph pixels were visually inspected. The direct character-specific Xiao Xue Tang asset URL could not be confirmed, although its licensing page does authorize queried glyph images under CC0.

No usable candidate image was established with both a direct image URL and verified rights. The described SFTJ page offers possible forms, but its reuse terms were not found; Commons searches returned unrelated character files.

No accessible primary facsimile or diplomatic transcription of the 集成04315 半 graph was inspected. The museum confirms later added Qin-Han text and scholarly disagreement on the vessel's date; attribution of the particular graph to the original Spring and Autumn inscription therefore remains dependent on the character databases.
The inspected textual pages do not establish an oracle-bone form. The absence of a displayed form is not proof of absence from the paleographic record.

CUHK calls 八 both semantic and phonetic, but Baxter–Sagart forms for 八 (*pˤret) and 半 (*pˤan-s) differ in the final. The sound-component assignment is a source claim, and the particular correspondence needs further explanation.
The proposal that 半 is 判's initial graph is attributed by CUHK to 何琳儀; the original publication and its full paleographic/phonological argument were not inspected.

The proposed original sense ‘split/open’ and extension ‘half’ are reported by CUHK and align with Shuowen's received explanation, but no dated series establishes when these word senses arose. Do not infer chronology from gloss ordering.

The Mawangdui 半-for-磐 borrowing is reported by CUHK. Its exact manuscript line was not checked against a facsimile; early independent attestations and historical sound comparison for 磐/盤 remain unverified.
The Proto-Sino-Tibetan *par and 半–畔 endopassive analyses in the dossier were not established by primary or specialist sources inspected here.

The historical record of uses as a fraction, middle-point, incomplete/partial, and ‘very little’ was sampled through dictionaries and citations. Dated first occurrences and semantic links between these uses remain unresolved.

Modern readings were checked selectively: Mandarin bàn, Cantonese bun3, Japanese on-reading はん, Korean 반, and Vietnamese bán appear in a secondary compilation. Their introduction dates and fuller regional variation were not researched.

One query for the ctext dictionary page returned an internal access error; guessed Academia Sinica font-code asset pages also returned inaccessible errors. No claims were taken from their snippets beyond identifying attempted URLs.
The sources inspected do not date a transition between ‘split/open’ and ‘half’; retain the sequence as unresolved.
The Baxter–Sagart sound comparison does not by itself demonstrate the proposed phonetic role of 八. The entry’s assignment remains a source assertion whose correspondence is not fully explained here.

No candidate image met the requirements for a direct image URL, character-specific historical identity, and inspected reuse provenance. The Commons result is a modern Cangjie instructional example; its file page could not be opened to check rights or image contents.
Historical bronze and Small Seal forms are described in the dossier sources, but no candidate image is supplied here because the specific pixels and direct asset endpoint were not inspected.

Suggested learner wording to resolve the review: overview should say that one account links “split” and “half,” while their sequence remains unresolved. For 八, explain that the similar beginnings permit a possible sound relationship, but the different endings leave its proposed sound role uncertain. The reconstruction comparison is cited in evidence above.

The Mawangdui manuscript’s exact date, line reading, and 半 token were not independently checked against a facsimile or accessible diplomatic transcription; the wording and correspondence are reported by the CUHK character database.

The sources establish plausible sound resemblance only across different reconstruction systems (半 Baxter–Sagart *pˤan-s; 磐 Zhengzhang *baːn). No same-system reconstruction comparison for both words was verified in this pass, and the precise sound basis for the Han-period spelling remains unresolved.

The character database identifies the word written 磐 in the received line and connects it to 盤桓, but does not separately establish the earliest attestations of the spoken words 磐 and 盤桓 or the token’s pronunciation at the time of borrowing.

The cited Mawangdui wording has secondary textual corroboration, but no primary facsimile or diplomatic transcription was inspected here; the token reading remains reported rather than independently checked against the manuscript.

The proposed sound-loan mechanism for 半 written for 磐 remains unproven. The received word 磐 and the graph 半 have plausible labial and -an similarities in separate reconstructions from the dossier, but no same-system comparison or direct reconstruction of the manuscript token establishes the precise Han-period sound match. The spoken source word and the pronunciation of the graph 半 must remain distinct questions.

The reviewer’s factual correction is supported: describe 牛-to-斗/升 and 斗-to-刃 as reported variant relationships, without implying a fully established chronology.

The reviewer’s readability correction is supported: state explicitly that the proposed semantic direction is “split/open” to “half,” while its sequence remains undated; identify the compared Old Chinese forms and note their differing endings.
